cards.text: A famine hits the land where Abram is living. And friend, it's a SEVERE one. So Abram decides to go down to another country and live there for a while.

cards.question: The famine is severe, so Abram goes down to another country to live there for a while. Which country?

cards.text: Right as he's about to enter Egypt, Abram turns to his wife Sarai and tells her he knows she's a beautiful woman. Smooth opener, Abram, but where is this GOING?

cards.question: Abram tells Sarai that when the Egyptians see her, they'll say, ‘This is his wife.’ What does Abram think they'll do next?

answers.text: Kill him but let her live

cards.text: Abram hasn't even crossed the border and he's already bracing for the worst. I KNOW that feeling, friend, because I did it every single time the drawer opened. So Abram asks Sarai to tell people she's something else to him.

cards.question: Abram asks Sarai to say she's his ___ instead of his wife.
Abram tells Sarai this plan will get him treated well for her sake.

cards.text: Abram walks into Egypt, and sure enough, the Egyptians see that Sarai is very beautiful. Then the officials of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, get a look at her too.

cards.question: Pharaoh's officials have seen Sarai. What do they do next?
After the officials praise her to Pharaoh, Sarai is taken into Pharaoh's ___.

cards.text: Meanwhile, Pharaoh treats Abram well on Sarai's account. Abram's plan is working, at least the part about Abram.

cards.question: While Sarai is in Pharaoh's palace, what does Abram end up with?

cards.text: Sheep and cattle, male AND female donkeys, menservants, maidservants and CAMELS. That's like crashing on a friend's couch for a while and somehow needing a MOVING TRUCK to leave.

cards.question: Sarai is Abram's wife, and she's living in Pharaoh's palace. What does the LORD do?

answers.text: Send an angel to bring Sarai out

cards.question: The LORD's severe plagues hit Pharaoh and nobody else in his household.

cards.text: Pharaoh summons Abram and asks, “What have you done to me? I bet Abram wishes he could crawl into a junk drawer right about now, and friend, I know a GOOD one.

cards.question: Besides “What have you done to me?” what else does Pharaoh want to know from Abram?

answers.text: Why Abram didn't say Sarai was his wife
Why Abram came down to Egypt at all
Why Abram brought so many people along

cards.text: Pharaoh says he took Sarai as his wife because Abram called her his sister. Then he hands her right back: “Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!”

cards.question: Pharaoh gives his men orders about Abram, and when they send him away, Abram has to leave his possessions behind.

cards.text: Out they go: Abram, Sarai and ALL his possessions, camels included. And that's where we'll leave them for now, friend, because this story is far from finished.

findings.problem: Abram is the first person to appear in this lesson, but the card never says who he is. It also doesn't give the opening context of where he is living, so the baker meets him with no introduction.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the bracing-for-the-worst line, the drawer joke and the request. Only the opening card may run to three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "this plan" points back to the sister plan from cards 5 and 6, which are no longer on screen. The question should name the plan, for example "saying Sarai is his sister."

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The joke about "needing a MOVING TRUCK to leave" tells the baker that Abram leaves Egypt with all his stuff. That gives away the answer to card 19, which asks whether Abram has to leave his possessions behind.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The quotation “What have you done to me? is opened but never closed, so Papa Dorin's own line ("I bet Abram wishes...") runs inside the Bible quote.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: In Genesis 12:19, Pharaoh asks a question ("Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife?"). The card turns that question into a statement with "Pharaoh says he took Sarai..."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line nearly copies the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
